title: ASML’s guidance key to instill confidence in fragile chip trade
article:
(Oct 13): ASML Holding NV’s guidance for building out capacity has become a crucial new part of the Dutch company’s earnings days, and will be even more so this time as investors seek signs of reassurance in the sector’s faltering rally.

After a stellar first-half, semiconductor stocks have come off the boil, with shares of South Korean chipmakers slumping to a two-month low on Tuesday, following a fresh slide in US names.

Investors will be looking to ASML and key client Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co (TSMC) to instill some confidence over the next 48 hours.

ASML, which reports before markets open on Wednesday, will be watched most closely for its outlook on fulfilling buoyant demand for its chipmaking equipment. Particularly so as it no longer publishes quarterly order numbers. TSMC releases results the following day.

“It is that capacity that is on the mind of the market and with no sight of order numbers, and a limited view of the backlog, it is vital that there is some sort of upgrade to its capacity targets,” said Ben Barringer, head of technology research at Quilter Cheviot.

See also: China’s CXMT claims memory advances ahead of Samsung, Hynix

While ASML has ceased giving quarterly order numbers, citing their “lumpy” nature, it has started sharing guidance for the number of machines expected to be built this year and beyond, one that’s increasingly used by investors to gauge the strength of demand and ASML’s ability to scale up supply.

In July, ASML said it plans to boost capacity by 30% next year for its second-most advanced tool, the low-NA extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography machine, which would take its annual shipment target to 85 units.

See also: Alibaba unveils US$450 smart glasses in expanding push into gadgets

Each of its low-NA tools costs roughly €200 million apiece and takes more than a year to deliver from the time of order. ASML said in July it is working to cut the time needed to build and test lithography tools at its factories by about a third.

But when it comes to 2028, there’s further uncertainty: ASML said it’s “investigating” whether another 30% capacity increase would be viable, without firmly committing to the target of about 110 tools.

Analysts are generally more bullish. The pace of capacity increases could go beyond 30% for both next year and the year after, according to UBS Group AG. Morgan Stanley sees ASML delivering more than 90 tools in 2027.

“If the client demand is higher, they would be able to raise the capacity numbers,” Bernstein’s David Dai said in an email. Still, the firm may keep its guidance unchanged for now before raising it three months later, because “demand will be much clearer then.”

Both ASML and TSMC appear conservative in ramping up their supply because “they’ve been burned before,” said Josep Bori, a global equity analyst at Aviva Investors. He sees an opportunity to add to the stock if it were to sell off on a lack of guidance upgrades.

Potential price increases are another focus. Chief financial officer Roger Dassen said in July there’s more flexibility to adjust pricing as productivity of its EUV tools rises. Later, The Information reported that the firm is planning a price hike, despite pushbacks from TSMC. Last week, South Korean publication The Elec reported that ASML is raising prices of replacement parts in the country by 10%.

To stay ahead of Singapore and the region’s corporate and economic trends, click here for Latest Section

Pricing can serve as another driver for revenue growth, in addition to more tools being sold. Analysts on average are forecasting a 28% increase in revenue for next year, on top of a 34% rise in 2026.

Bank of America estimates that ASML’s earnings will probably rise by 8% for every 5% increase in tools and servicing prices. Higher pricing could start to boost earnings toward the end of 2027, according to analysts led by Didier Scemama.

Trading at 32 times next year’s earnings, ASML’s premium versus US-listed peers Applied Materials Inc and Lam Research Corp is close to the lowest in over a decade.

Among hedge fund investors, the stock was viewed as one to short to fund purchases of other semiconductor shares, according to a JPMorgan Chase & Co trading desk note published last week.

Higher EUV capacity, stronger pricing and ultimately a more bullish medium-term framework may be necessary to drive further earnings upgrades, it said. “A lot of the bull case is now well understood,” the desk wrote.

title: China’s CXMT claims memory advances ahead of Samsung, Hynix
article:
(Oct 13): CXMT Corp declared it achieved a breakthrough in chip technology that rivals like Samsung Electronics Co had pursued for years, an unsubstantiated claim that jolted stocks and reflects China’s aggressive push into a critical sphere.

The domestic memory leader plans to roll out a new type of chips with increased memory density thanks to the company’s self-developed new architecture, CXMT president Cao Kanyu told an industry conference in Shanghai over the weekend. The upcoming product for data centre servers sports a so-called 4F² design and should launch before the end of the year, Cao said in comments confirmed by a company spokesperson.

If CXMT has succeeded in achieving the 4F² threshold, that means it got there before Samsung and SK Hynix Inc — despite US sanctions that bar the Chinese firm’s access to tools such as ASML Holding NV’s top-end machines. Cao didn’t provide more details, but the widely reported remarks helped spark a selloff in global chip stocks.

Samsung and SK Hynix shares fell 7.4% and 10%, respectively, in South Korea on Tuesday, weighing down the broader Kospi index, after Micron Technology Inc closed down 4% overnight.

“A successful and earlier implementation of 4F² architecture in DRAM production would vastly improve CXMT’s competitive position versus peers,” said Jing Jie Yu, an analyst with Morningstar. “That said, memory leaders as well as equipment manufacturers have both similarly echoed the difficulty in this technological transition, and we still expect a meaningful time gap between the unveiling of CXMT’s 4F² product and commercialisation at viable yields.”

See also: Alibaba unveils US$450 smart glasses in expanding push into gadgets

Cao’s declaration — months after CXMT briefly became China’s most valuable company following a blockbuster summer IPO — underscores its effort to close the gap with foreign rivals in the making of advanced memory chips, an area essential to artificial intelligence (AI) development.

The Chinese firm’s breakthrough shouldn’t pose an immediate threat to Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron’s dominance in high-bandwidth memory, a type of semiconductors that transfers massive amounts of data and is vital to Nvidia Corp AI accelerators.

See also: Apple needs phones and smart homes to revive pricey stock

But it shows how CXMT is incrementally closing the gap in technologies across the broader memory sphere. It’s already on track to produce the latest generation of smartphone memory chips, dubbed LPDDR6, in roughly the same timeline as Samsung and SK Hynix.

The industry’s existing 6F² standard refers to a surface area of 6-times the square of the “feature size” of a chip: the basic line-width between transistors. Samsung and SK Hynix are exploring ways to shrink that to 4F², in theory packing the same cells into a smaller area for greater efficiency.

CXMT’s Cao said it’s changing the way transistors are laid out to squeeze in more cells and hence expand memory density. The so-called Vertical Surrounding Gate approach should reduce leakage and other side effects — a problem long associated with efforts to reduce sizes beyond the 6F² standard.

If successful, CXMT would spearhead a breakaway from current design and techniques. Cao added his company has been working on this since its inception a decade ago, and now holds more patents in this area than rivals. Key to CXMT’s breakthrough was its ability to separate memory cell manufacturing from that of peripheral circuitry, Cao said.

Until now, manufacturers built those two components on the same piece of silicon. Under CXMT’s new technique, the two parts are manufactured on separate wafers, which are then combined using hybrid bonding technology.

It’s unclear what sorts of yields — the proportion of usable chips — CXMT has managed to achieve with that approach. It’s challenging to maintain uniformity in mass production, according to Morningstar’s Yu.

If it works, the new architecture marks the latest example of innovative workarounds that Chinese companies from Huawei Technologies Co to DeepSeek devise to get around US technology curbs. If CXMT succeeds in commercialising the technology, it may boost memory density in the company’s products by 30%, giving it an edge over Samsung and SK Hynix, Yu said.

To stay ahead of Singapore and the region’s corporate and economic trends, click here for Latest Section

“In reality, while the Chinese memory makers can potentially become a threat to global demand-supply balance over time, in the short run they continue to face technology hurdles,” said Vey-Sern Ling, a managing director at Union Bancaire Privee.

Huawei in May unveiled its Tau Scaling Law, an alternative to the decades-old Moore’s Law of shrinking transistors to boost chip performance. The Chinese chip champion instead seeks to speed up transmission and increase transistor density within a chip through LogicFolding. It’s already rolled out chips using this technology that run on smartphones launched this year.

CXMT is racing to ramp up production of advanced memory to meet surging AI demand. The ability to manufacture sophisticated products would also position the company better as a global supply crunch begins to ease in coming years.

It remains a laggard in high-bandwidth memory. Still, it’s making steady progress in the broader DRAM market. The company’s share of that field had expanded to 10% by the second quarter of this year, compared to just 4% a year ago, data compiled by Counterpoint Research shows.

“If CXMT manufactures products using its 4F² architecture by the end of 2026, it will be a significant milestone. However, stabilising mass production yields and securing commercial supply scale for this new technology will be key,” said Jeongku Choi, a senior analyst at Counterpoint Research.

It may “serve as a good example demonstrating the increased self-reliance and technological level of the Chinese semiconductor ecosystem.”

title: BOJ to lean against back-to-back rate hike in October — Bloomberg
article:
(Oct 13): Bank of Japan (BOJ) officials are leaning against a rare back-to-back interest rate increase this month while still eyeing the possibility of another move as soon as December, according to people familiar with the matter.

The BOJ officials see little need for consecutive rate hikes in the absence of signs that upside inflation risks will increase abruptly, the people said. The central bank will instead carefully examine economic data to see if another hike is warranted as early as the December gathering, the people said.

The final policy decision at the Oct 30 meeting could still change until the last minute, the people said.

Governor Kazuo Ueda’s board lifted borrowing costs to 1.25% last month as it looked to keep on top of upside inflation risks. The move also came amid a wave of pressure from Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent to keep normalising policy and help strengthen the yen.

The yen initially weakened after this report before regaining ground to trade around 157.08 per dollar early Tuesday evening in Tokyo.

The September rate increase was the second in three months, the fastest pace of hikes since 1990. Ueda said that move was warranted as the BOJ shifted to a new policy phase with more focus on upside price risks. Still, the BOJ hasn’t pushed up rates in consecutive months since 1980, an indication of a deeply held preference for monitoring the impact of policy moves before acting again.

See also: Topix’s biggest ever revamp to cull hundreds of Japan stocks

Pricing in the overnight swaps market shows that traders are pricing in a roughly 10% probability of a hike this month, with the chances rising to 88% for a move by December. About a third of economists polled last month forecast a move in December, with more than half predicting the BOJ would wait until January.

Japan’s economy and inflation have been developing in line with the BOJ’s outlook more or less, the people said. The price trend is expected to be consistent with the 2% target sometime in the next 18 months.

While underlying inflation can finally be assessed as being around 2%, more than a decade after the target was set in 2013, that doesn’t mean the bank’s mission is accomplished. The goal is not merely to hit 2%, but to make inflation stabilise around that level, the people said.

See also: Suzuki undercuts BYD as competition for cheap mini EVs heats up

Ueda touched on that point Tuesday, saying it was vital to stabilise the price trend around 2%, during comments he made in parliament.

With underlying inflation around the bank’s target, the BOJ will keep looking for the right timing for another rate increase while assessing the impact of its hikes so far, the people said.

The bank will release a new quarterly economic outlook along with its policy statement. Officials will weigh the impact of elevated oil prices and whether the bank needs to factor in a pending temporary cut in sales tax on food into their forecasts, according to the people.

For the time being, inflationary pressure from input costs has cooled a touch, according to producer price data for September released earlier in the day. The slowing of gains suggests no urgent need to stop prices accelerating out of control. Still, at 6.8% they support the BOJ pushing up rates in due course.

The BOJ has pledged to closely monitor the development in the Middle East, AI-related demand and foreign exchange rates to decide the timing of a rate hike.

Market bets for a BOJ October rate hike reached around 40% at one point late last month. But with investors no longer expecting a rate hike by the Federal Reserve (Fed) this month after clear signals from Fed officials, those expectations weakened. Still, US CPI data this week will be a key focus among traders.

Oil prices have risen about 15% since the BOJ compiled the latest quarterly economic projection late July, fanning inflationary pressures for the nation heavily reliant on imports of natural resources.

Japan’s currency is still weaker compared with the 155.87 level it marked hours before the BOJ raised borrowing costs by a quarter-point on Sept 18. Japan’s Finance Ministry and US Treasury Department conducted a highly unusual joint intervention to prop up the yen at the end of July. Bessent has become even more vocal about BOJ policy since then.

title: Jio Platforms said to draw more than US$20 bil in bids for IPO in India
article:
(Oct 13): Jio Platforms Ltd has drawn more than US$20 billion in bids for what could be India’s biggest-ever initial public offering, according to people familiar with the matter.

Global investors, including Fidelity, Allianz and Capital Group, as well as other international and local firms have indicated interest in the IPO, some of the people said, asking not to be identified because the information is private.

A final list of IPO anchor investors will likely be decided in the coming days, the people said, adding that the process is ongoing and no final decisions have been made yet.

Representatives for Jio’s parent Reliance Industries Ltd and Fidelity did not respond to requests for comment. Allianz and Capital Group declined to comment.

After earlier expectations reached as high as US$170 billion, Jio Platforms is now aiming for a valuation of as much as 10.3 trillion rupees in the IPO, people familiar with the matter have said.

Akash Ambani, the 34-year-old managing director of Jio Platforms and son of multibillionaire Mukesh, has been leading the deal with meetings from Hong Kong to London and New York in recent weeks. According to people in attendance, investors pressed Ambani and his team on the valuation target and how the company plans to charge for digital services and various platforms.

The share sale is expected to open next week for an IPO before Oct 30.

None of Jio Platforms’ investors, which include Meta Platforms Inc, Alphabet Inc, Mubadala and Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund, are looking to exit in the IPO, as the offering is entirely a primary issue, the draft prospectus shows.

At the upper end of the price band, Jio Platforms’ IPO would raise about 302 billion rupees, according to Bloomberg calculations. India’s biggest IPO to date was by Hyundai Motor Co’s local unit, which raised about 279 billion rupees in 2024.

title: Alibaba unveils US$450 smart glasses in expanding push into gadgets
article:
(Oct 13): Alibaba Group Holding Ltd on Tuesday unveiled the new generation of its smart glasses, deepening its foray into consumer electronics as an extension of its artificial intelligence (AI) strategy.

The company, which models itself as China’s full-stack AI provider spanning everything from data centres and software to end-user products, detailed its new Qwen Glasses N1 series at an event in Hangzhou. With prices starting at 2,999 yuan (US$450) before discounts, they’re no cheaper than industry leader Meta Platforms Inc’s Ray-Ban smart glasses, showing Alibaba’s effort to compete on quality and features rather than just price.

Mirroring Meta’s strategy, Alibaba is endeavouring to turn smart glasses into an entry point for its AI tools and agents. Meta last month expanded its lineup of smart glasses with a simplified, camera-free model priced at US$349, designed primarily for interaction with the new Muse AI assistant.

The new Alibaba glasses include improved 50-megapixel cameras and sensors, with a Pro edition priced at 3,499 yuan featuring new eye-tracking functions, said Wu Jianjun, general manager of Qwen AI hardware products. The new glasses will offer 25 hours of standby time or nine hours of music playback from one charge, Alibaba said. Coming roughly a year after November’s first edition, the new glasses more tightly integrate Alibaba’s Qwen AI assistant and expand on its functionality.

Users will be able to speak to the AI agent via bone-conduction microphones, and the glasses also support shopping functions, payments and health tracking. Alibaba chief executive officer Eddie Wu last month reiterated the company’s ambition to develop all-stack AI, from large language models and chatbot apps to AI chips and hardware.

To provide a more affordable way to access Qwen, Alibaba also started sales of its new AI earbuds named Qwen Clip. These were jointly developed with headphone maker Bose Corp and are priced at 1,299 yuan.

See also: Apple needs phones and smart homes to revive pricey stock

title: Apple needs phones and smart homes to revive pricey stock
article:
(Oct 13): Apple Inc is rolling out a slew of new products and improved older ones this week, but investors are unsure if it will be enough to boost one of the most expensive stocks in the market that’s largely gone nowhere in months.

The iPhone maker is holding a smart-home products event on Tuesday featuring an Apple doorbell and Apple thermostat, according to a Bloomberg News report. Later this month, the company is planning to launch a touchscreen MacBook and a new iPad mini. And on Friday, pre-orders begin for the new foldable iPhone Duo, which represents the biggest design change in the history of Apple’s most profitable device and carries a commensurately hefty price tag.

The stakes are high for Apple shares, which soared to a record in late July amid reports about its push into the smart-home market and scepticism about heavy artificial intelligence (AI) spending that Apple has avoided. But the stock is basically flat in the months since.

“For a company of this size, you need super-hit products to move the needle on growth,” said Peter Andersen, who helps oversee US$5.5 billion as chief investment officer of Andersen Capital Management. “I’m just not sure anything we’re getting is exciting enough to lead to an inflection.”

The stock is up 25% this year, making Apple the top performer among the Magnificent Seven tech giants. It trades at more than 35 times earnings estimated over the next 12 months, right around its highest multiple since 2007 and well above its 10-year average of 24. Apple is among the 50 most expensive stocks in the S&P 500 Index, which is priced at 19 times forward earnings.

See also: Chip sell-off triggers 7% Korea rout after CEO’s ‘casino’ warning

Some of that reflects Apple’s unique position within the AI trade, where it isn’t exposed to spending risk but is considered a key beneficiary of the technology’s development. And it shows investors’ high expectations for new chief executive officer John Ternus and their hopes that he can generate growth by upgrading and expanding its lineup of devices.

That’s a risk, however. The company has cut component orders for some iPhone models due to weaker-than-expected demand, according to a Bloomberg Intelligence report last week. Meanwhile, consumers are feeling pressured by stubborn inflation, and Apple has had to raise prices due to higher costs for components like memory chips.

See also: China’s CXMT claims memory breakthrough ahead of Samsung, Hynix

“Apple executes its products flawlessly, but it’s hard to expect these will really take off,” said Andersen, who doesn’t own the stock, in part due to what he sees as the company’s lack of innovation. “Not only have there been major players in the home market for years, but Apple is launching these products into a market where consumers are under a lot of pressure.”

What’s more, Apple’s growth rate is lagging its Big Tech peers, making its high stock market valuation stand out even more than it already does. The company’s fiscal year ended on Sept 30, and it’s projected to post a 15% rise in annual revenue when it reports earnings in a few weeks. But that appears to be a near-peak, with the pace expected to slow to 10% in fiscal 2027 and 7.8% in fiscal 2028.

“Apple doesn’t look like a value stock or a growth stock,” Andersen said. “Given where the multiple is, it seems questionable to expect much additional stock upside from here.”

Of course, Apple isn’t alone in its slowing growth. Overall tech sales are expected to experience a deceleration in the coming years, albeit off a much higher level. Revenue is projected to climb 37% for the S&P 500 information tech sector in 2026, and 29% in 2027, according to Bloomberg Intelligence.

Whether Apple’s new products will alter the company’s earnings outlook remains to be seen. But Wall Street hasn’t been racing to adjust its projections. Analysts’ expectations for the company’s fiscal 2027 net income have dipped by 0.6% over the past three months, while their view for revenue has risen 0.7%.

“Apple’s product path seems promising, but I don’t think the first generation of new products will mean much for overall revenue,” said Lu Zhang, founder and managing partner of Fusion Fund, who owns the stock in her personal portfolio. “It remains to be seen whether we will see the kind of new use cases [for the foldable Duo] that will contribute to a broad upgrade cycle.”

Nevertheless, Zhang remains positive on the stock. Apple could improve its AI offerings, she said, but it will continue to benefit from being a gateway for consumers to access the emerging technology.

“All the AI companies are competing with each other, but whenever they launch a new model they need Apple as a key distribution channel, and that’s an area where it essentially has no competitor,” she said. “Even if Duo adoption isn’t high right out of the gate, so long as Apple continues to execute on its hardware, it will warrant a premiere multiple.”

title: Chip sell-off triggers 7% Korea rout after CEO’s ‘casino’ warning
article:
(Oct 13): A global slide in semiconductor stocks deepened, sending South Korea’s chip-heavy equity benchmark down more than 7% at one point, as concerns about AI overheating and Chinese competition intensified.

Samsung Electronics Co and SK Hynix Inc shares dropped about 7% and 10% each Tuesday, dragging the Kospi down 5.5% at the close. Taiwan’s Taiex and Japan’s Nikkei 225 both fell nearly 2% after US chipmakers slumped overnight.

Investor angst over the AI trade increased after Broadcom Inc’s chief executive likened market sentiment to a casino and warned that financing the buildout will become a key problem. That further undermined the case for AI stocks, just as higher interest rates begin to take a toll on massive debt-funded deals and threaten once-hot initial public offerings.

“Uncertainty over whether the upcycle can last into 2028 and beyond appears to be weighing on valuations and share prices” of Korean chipmakers, said Ha SeokKeun, chief investment officer at Eugene Asset Management.

Korean stocks took the biggest hit, as investors also reacted to a report that Chinese rival CXMT Corp has made progress on a new memory architecture that Samsung and SK Hynix are also working on. The Seoul stock exchange briefly halted Kospi programme trading for the first time since August.

See also: China’s CXMT claims memory breakthrough ahead of Samsung, Hynix

The Kospi is now down a third from the record high it reached in June and below its 200-day moving average. Foreigners have accelerated their exit, selling US$3.4 billion ($4.3 billion) worth of Kospi shares Tuesday, the most since June.

CXMT plans to roll out a new server-memory product by the end of 2026 that enables higher storage density, according to a report from South China Morning Post on Monday. That resurfaced fears of rapid development by Chinese chipmakers that have rattled global rivals this year.

Record earnings from Samsung last week failed to give the stock a boost.

See also: Microsoft bets on homegrown Maia AI chip to challenge Nvidia

“Samsung’s strong earnings have been overshadowed by concerns about future competition from CXMT and the sustainability of AI spending,” said Jung In Yun, chief executive officer at Fibonacci Asset Management Global. “These concerns may weigh on sentiment, but CXMT still needs to translate technological progress into commercially competitive production at scale.”

Broader worry over the longevity of the AI boom continues to weigh on industry stocks after last week’s collapse of a planned offering by Nvidia Corp-backed data centre company Firmus Grid Ltd.

Broadcom CEO Hock Tan said financing may be a bigger problem than chip shortages. “A lot of investors have no clue what they are investing in,” the head of the American chipmaker said at an event in Singapore. They “set very extreme expectations only to find out that it’s almost like they are in a casino.”

This week’s earnings from ASML Holding NV and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co will help investors gauge how long bumper profit growth can last. Shares of TSMC, Asia’s most-valuable company, slipped 2% Tuesday.

“Traders aren’t treating good news stories or lofty valuations as gospel any more, they’re digging much more carefully into the numbers and the underlying business case, with the whole AI trade still under the microscope,” said Tim Waterer, chief market analyst at KCM Trade.

title: NYSE owner plans futures for livestock in a bid to challenge CME Group
article:
(Oct 13): Intercontinental Exchange Inc, owner of the New York Stock Exchange, is planning to offer contracts for betting on future cattle and hog prices, competing with long-time incumbent CME Group Inc as it moves its systems to the cloud.

The first cattle and hogs futures contracts will be listed before the end of the year, targeting a Dec 7 launch, according to ICE executives. The exchange operator will offer physically settled cattle futures as well as three cash-settled contracts for cattle and hog prices, all pending regulatory review.

CME, the largest US futures exchange, is moving its matching engine for certain instruments to a new Google Cloud data centre. In response, ICE is looking to shake up the industry by providing another option to hedge.

“We received significant inbound customer demand from those seeking credible alternatives to what has historically been a singular choice for cattle,” Trabue Bland, ICE’s senior vice president of futures markets, said in a statement.

The debate over CME’s move to the cloud has intensified among trading firms and the agriculture community since the exchange announced its plans for the new system, which was slated to be located in Dallas, according to people familiar with the matter who asked not to be identified discussing a private matter. Some firms have expressed concern that the shift might increase costs and slow trading speeds, two of the people said.

Chicago-based CME, which has offered cattle and hog trading since the 1960s, has previously said that moving its tech infrastructure to the cloud can help it control costs, create real-time analytical capabilities and increase efficiencies. Outgoing Chief Executive Officer Terry Duffy has said he would not put products in the cloud unless they are “better than what I have today.”

See also: S&P 500 hovers near all-time high before earnings

CME said Monday in a statement that a previously disclosed move of its livestock markets to Dallas won’t have to go along as planned, since a newly built data centre in Aurora, Illinois, is coming online faster than expected.

Dallas will still have a disaster recovery facility but the interim move of the primary market will no longer be required, a company representative said.

See also: Goldman strategists upgrade global stocks on earnings boost

CME has contracts for both younger feeder animals and mature live cattle that are ready for processing. Those futures prices have skyrocketed in recent years as the US herd shrank to its smallest size in over half a century, pressuring margins for meat processors and some ranchers.

Managing beef prices has been a key focus for restaurants and retailers as the protein remains an outsize driver of food inflation. Stores have trimmed serving sizes, turned to cheaper cuts or promoted other proteins while the Trump administration has been trying to boost foreign supplies in an effort to tamp down prices.

Exchanges in the US and abroad are racing to list products that give investors new ways to hedge risks. CME has listed new instruments for protecting against price movements on livestock items such as beef. ICE is sending out a notice to members this week to announce its new, alternative contracts, which will be listed under the codes COW, MOO and SOW.

“There are moments in time in the evolution of markets where choice becomes a compelling motivation and we believe this is an inflection point for the industry as we work to launch a cattle futures market,” Bland said.

title: LVMH’s China slump threatens hopes for wider luxury recovery
article:
(Oct 13): LVMH Moët Hennessy Louis Vuitton SE offered a closer look at the deepening Chinese luxury slump this week, revealing that sales on the mainland dropped by double digits in the third quarter while the traditionally high-spending consumer group also pulled back overseas.

The weak spending contributed to a 5% drop in organic revenue in the Asia excluding Japan segment, the only region where the luxury giant saw a year-on-year decline. Chinese shoppers’ purchases overseas declined by a mid-single-digit percentage while overall demand improved later in the quarter ending Sept 30, chief financial officer Cecile Cabanis told analysts on a call.

The China slowdown at LVMH, long seen as an industry bellwether, adds to doubts about the durability of a broader luxury recovery and could offer a worrying signal for rivals, including Yves Saint Laurent owner Kering SA and Hermès International SCA, which are due to report earnings later this month. China had helped fuel an industry rebound less than a year ago but worsening economic sentiment is again weighing on high-end spending.

“The news flow has not been particularly good in China in the summer,” Cabanis said. “So this has really weighed on the feel-good factor and created a short-term subdued Chinese backdrop.”

LVMH shares were little changed in early Paris trading, after declining about 40% this year.

See also: Luxury condos seized in Singapore’s biggest money-laundering case find few buyers

Luxury demand in China is being squeezed on numerous fronts. Consumer wariness amid a broader economic slowdown is restraining spending at home and pushing some shoppers toward cheaper local brands. At the same time, recent stock-market weakness and tougher taxation of overseas wealth are weighing on some of the country’s richest consumers.

“Everybody’s having a tough time,” said Jacques Roizen, co-founder of Shanghai-based consultancy Foresight Performance Partners. “LVMH as a portfolio of scale is such an industry index and the other luxury listed companies are not going to significantly outperform that.”

The slowdown in Chinese demand contrasted with spending by US customers, which rose by a mid-single-digit percentage.

See also: Louis Vuitton loses sales in China after tea logo case backlash

Louis Vuitton also faced public backlash after a trademark dispute with local tea chain Molly Tea stirred criticism in China during the quarter, adding to pressure on LVMH’s biggest label. Cabanis said that while it was difficult to quantify the impact, the consumer pushback hurt Louis Vuitton at least at the beginning of the period.

The setback in China comes as the broader luxury recovery faces pressure from conflict in the Middle East and cost-of-living concerns that are curbing discretionary spending globally.

That pressure is already showing across the luxury sector. Sales at the 25 biggest luxury labels in China dropped more than 10% in July, Bloomberg reported earlier. That threatens to derail a recovery that began less than a year ago, when a stock market boom fuelled by artificial intelligence helped revive luxury spending.

LVMH’s renewed gains in revenue and earnings per share this year “grew precarious” as China’s slowdown deepened in the third quarter, Bloomberg Intelligence analysts Deborah Aitken and Karine Pitton wrote.

“There was a shift in the Chinese consumer backdrop, and this forces us to sharpen our self-help effort,” CFO Cabanis said. “We need to do more but we have not stopped investing in China.”

title: Hong Kong lifeline buys Cheng family time to save New World
article:
(Oct 13): It was a Wednesday evening in late September and analysts covering New World Development Co were getting antsy. The cash-strapped Hong Kong developer was late to report its earnings and executives had not shown up to a scheduled briefing.

Behind the scenes, New World was scrambling to hammer out a deal that, when announced hours later, would give it a crucial lifeline, according to people familiar with the matter. Hong Kong’s Airport Authority agreed to waive billions of dollars in rent the company had committed to pay for its struggling 11 Skies project near the airport, alleviating its debt burden.

In return, the Airport Authority would fully take over the HK$18 billion mega mall-and-office complex — and get an option to buy a significant chunk of the developer’s shares at a steep discount. The agreement came with a key condition: the founding Cheng family must remain New World’s largest shareholder.

The unusual deal shows how far Hong Kong authorities are prepared to go to stabilise one of the city’s biggest property developers as New World faces nearly US$11 billion of debt coming due as early as next year. It buys the billionaire Cheng family more time to shore up a company that posted a record US$3.6 billion loss in its recent fiscal year.

New World will also give HK$3 billion in cash and services to the Airport Authority as part of the agreement.

The pseudo-bailout sends a clear message: the city’s property tycoons, who have built Hong Kong into what it is today but are also responsible for sustaining one of the world’s most expensive and inequitable property markets, are too big to fail.

See also: Six-storey commercial building at Middle Road for sale at $80 mil

“The deal highlights New World’s economic and policy relevance to Hong Kong, particularly as the government pushes ahead” with an ambitious plan to develop a new area in the northern part of the city that needs support from developers, said Gary Ng, senior economist at Natixis. “Further financial pressure on New World could increase restructuring or default risks.”

Representatives for New World and the Cheng family did not respond to requests for comment. The Airport Authority declined to comment beyond its earlier announcement on the 11 Skies agreement, which said the project paves the way for further development of the airport area.

New World shares were flat in Hong Kong trading Tuesday afternoon. The stock has fallen nearly 29% this year, compared with a 5.4% drop in the benchmark Hang Seng Index.

See also: 999-year strata-titled shophouse in Binjai Park for sale at $4.4 mil

The 11 Skies agreement also gives the Chengs breathing room to act on New World’s capital structure — until late 2029. As part of the deal, the Airport Authority can buy 750 million New World shares — about a 30% stake — from the family’s investment arm Chow Tai Fook Enterprises Ltd within three years for HK$2.25 billion, which amounts to about a roughly 43% discount to the developer’s current share price.

But since the option is conditional on Chow Tai Fook remaining New World’s largest shareholder, the Cheng family will need to inject fresh capital or expand New World’s equity base before the Airport Authority can exercise its right.

The 11 Skies exit represents “a great leap toward equity raising” and may implicitly signal an equity deal within three years, UBS Group AG analysts including Mark Leung wrote this month.

Investors hope that the deal will inject momentum into talks between the Chengs and a variety of co-investment partners that have dragged on for more than a year, amid the family’s reluctance to cede power.

Most recently, the Chengs discussed a potential investment with Bain Capital, separate people familiar with the matter said. But macroeconomic uncertainty has made both the investor and the family more cautious about a deal.

Discussions with Blackstone Inc over a US$4 billion tie-up ended earlier this year after the Cheng family refused to give up control of the company, people familiar said in May.

The overlap between New World’s fortunes and the Hong Kong government’s ambitions has deep roots. During the city’s property downturn in the 1980s, New World pressed ahead with major investments — like the landmark Convention and Exhibition Centre — to help boost confidence. The Chengs have also been enthusiastic investors in mainland China, including on infrastructure and urban redevelopment projects.

Local regulators have also taken an interest in New World’s stability. When the developer was trying to refinance a record amount of debt last year, Hong Kong Monetary Authority officials contacted lenders directly before a rollover agreement was reached days before the deadline.

The economic backdrop has become less favourable in the past year. China’s efforts to claw back tax revenue from wealthy citizens’ overseas assets and higher interest rates in Hong Kong could threaten the city’s nascent property recovery, which had been one of the few tailwinds for New World.

In the meantime, the Chengs are leaning on other liquidity measures, including debt swaps and extending loan maturities. New World has announced an exchange offer for about US$991 million in bonds due in 2027 and 2028, following a previous 3.24 billion yuan asset spin-off in Shanghai.

“The Cheng family has been working assiduously to repair New World’s finances but has yet to put any of its additional private capital at risk,” said Brock Silvers, managing director at private equity firm Kaiyuan Capital. “That may soon change.”

title: Copper and aluminium drop as AI selloff saps appetite for risk
article:
(Oct 13): Copper and aluminium retreated as investor angst around overheated spending on artificial-intelligence infrastructure fuelled uncertainty about the demand outlook for the metals.

AI and technology stocks dropped across global markets following warnings the rapid buildout of data centres will become more difficult to finance. South Korea’s equity benchmark — which has been correlated with copper prices at times this year — slumped as much as 7%.

Copper bulls argue that AI infrastructure will be a key source of demand in the coming decade and any doubts about the pace of spending can hit trading sentiment. Still, the major driver for the red metal’s 17% rally this year has been the threat of US import tariffs, which has pulled huge volumes into the country and cut availability elsewhere.

“While not acting as the sole rationale behind the copper price performance in 2026 thus far, AI-driven sentiment is expected to continue to shape, if not dominate, the narrative in the coming years,” BMI, a Fitch Solutions company, said in a note.

Copper fell 0.2% to US$14,588 a tonne on the London Metal Exchange as of 11.25am in Shanghai. Aluminium, which is also used in AI infrastructure, dropped 0.3% and zinc lost 0.7%. Iron ore declined 0.3% to US$90.70 a tonne in Singapore, touching the lowest level in two years.

title: India’s rupee gains most in Asia as RBI widens currency curbs
article:
(Oct 13): India’s rupee extended gains as the central bank widened currency curbs to support the rupee, which faces pressure from high oil prices and foreign outflows.

The rupee outperformed Asian peers Tuesday, rising as much as 0.8% to 95.01 per dollar, following Monday’s 1% gain, as the Reserve Bank of India extended curbs on certain types of derivative transactions to avoid pressuring the currency.

“The negative bias for the rupee has turned, at least for now,” said Dilip Parmar, currency analyst at HDFC Securities. The accelerated strength in the currency is being driven by an unwinding of positions that were earlier exerting strain on the rupee, with liquidity also thinner, he said.

The range for now is 95.10-96 per dollar, he said, adding that a break on the stronger side could take the currency to 94.50.

The central bank backed up its regulatory measures with currency-market interventions that further boosted the rupee’s gains on Tuesday, according to traders familiar with the developments. The currency is still down more than 5% this year, ranking as one of Asia’s weaker performers.

See also: Goldman says markets underestimating how far yuan can rise

The series of regulatory interventions over the past few days highlight the RBI’s resolve to rein in the rupee’s weakness after its first interest-rate increase in nearly four years did little to alter the currency’s course. It also shows that elevated oil prices and persistent foreign outflows from local stocks are keeping policymakers on guard against further depreciation.

Late Monday, the RBI said that banks with operating units in the International Financial Services Centre can only offer offshore rupee-linked derivatives to non-residents for the purpose of hedging. It also widened the scope of a newly-introduced foreign-exchange risk reserve, making it applicable for banks’ own assets and liabilities.

The moves add to steps taken over the weekend, including a special window for oil firms’ dollar demand and broad restrictions on derivatives markets. These represent the strongest rupee-defence measures taken by the RBI since the 2013 taper tantrum episode, with the currency marking several fresh lows over the past year.

See also: South Korean won hits two-year high on lower oil, dollar sales

“Currency-market arbitrage has anyway been pretty much neutralised and the fresh restrictions are another step in that direction,” said Kunal Sodhani, head of treasury at Shinhan Bank in Mumbai, referring to transactions where traders profit from price differences in the onshore and offshore markets.

“These measures are primarily designed to manage market behaviour and volatility,” he said.

Still, there are some who forecast further weakness for the rupee. The currency will gradually weaken to 97.50 per dollar by the September quarter next year, Michael Wan, senior currency analyst at MUFG Bank in Singapore, wrote in a note.

title: Crypto wallet tampering fallout widens as OneKey drops Malaysian reseller
article:
(Oct 13): Crypto hardware maker OneKey has revoked CryptoBilis’s authorisation as a reseller of its products, widening the fallout from the discovery that some Ledger wallets sold through the Malaysian retailer had funds stolen.

“We have no reports of OneKey users losing assets in this incident but we are acting as if the risk is real,” Hong Kong-based OneKey said in a statement on its website. “CryptoBilis is no longer an authorised OneKey reseller.”

Paris-based Ledger SAS said it is investigating reports that users lost funds after buying its hardware wallets through CryptoBilis. The on-chain research group YFarmX estimates that as much as US$103 million was stolen. Ledger has not confirmed the amount lost but said it verified that one affected user’s device contained an unauthorised hardware implant.

The incident is the latest in a series of attacks to plague the crypto industry in recent months, including the theft of more than US$100 million in bitcoin from Coldcard-branded wallets made by Canada-based Coinkite Inc. Hardware wallets, commonly used for cold storage, are considered among the more secure methods of holding cryptocurrency because they use physical devices to store private keys offline.

CryptoBilis said on Oct 10 it had paused the sale and shipment of all hardware wallets across its stores and online channels in Malaysia, the Philippines and Indonesia.

“We are doing this as a precaution, to protect our customers while Ledger’s investigation continues and while we review our own processes with the help of independent specialists,” it said in a post on X.

See also: Singapore Bitcoin investors seek more returns but prioritise control

Following the reports, CryptoBilis co-founder Arravind Prabu posted on LinkedIn that the reseller was acquired earlier this year and that management responsibilities were handed over in March. CryptoBilis didn’t immediately respond to an emailed request for comment.

Ledger said the number of impacted devices is limited and it is working with relevant authorities.

“We know this is concerning, especially for those directly affected and we are reaching out to impacted users,” it said in a post on X. All confirmed cases related to the incident involve devices sold through CryptoBilis, it added.

See also: Bitcoin falls as US$600 mil in risky crypto bets wiped out

OneKey said devices bought from CryptoBilis between March 1 and Oct 12 can be replaced for free. It has also stopped onboarding new resellers and will review existing ones, it said.

OneKey, a rival to hardware-wallet makers Ledger and Trezor, is backed by Coinbase Ventures and YZi Labs, the family office of Binance Holdings co-founders Changpeng Zhao and Yi He.

title: Visa approved to prepare domestic payments business in China
article:
(Oct 13): Visa Inc received approval to begin preparations to establish a domestic bank card clearing business in China, as the firm follows rivals Mastercard Inc and American Express Co in serving the country’s massive payments market.

“We greatly appreciate the important role of the leaders of the United States and China in pursuing a constructive and strategically stable relationship between the world’s largest economies,” Visa CEO Ryan McInerney said in the statement.

The company’s Beijing unit won the green light from the People’s Bank of China, the official Xinhua News Agency reported Tuesday. It must complete preparatory work within one year before applying to commence operations and obtaining the clearing business licence, Xinhua added.

Visa’s clearance of the regulatory hurdle will allow it to operate in China’s US$144 trillion payments market and mark the end of its years-long pursuit. Visa applied for the licence in 2017, local media reported. Competitor Mastercard received approval to establish its bank card clearing business in 2020 and Amex’s joint venture in the country was approved to start bank card clearing services several months after that.

For years, the battle for entry into mainland China’s massive domestic clearing market was a primary friction point in the broader trade dispute between the world’s two largest economies.

Earlier this year, US President Donald Trump said he brought up Visa’s request for access to mainland China’s market during a meeting with Xi Jinping in Beijing. Visa’s CEO McInerney accompanied Trump on that May trip to China. Xi later met his counterpart in Washington in late September, with both agreeing on a trade truce extension. The two are scheduled to talk again in person on the sidelines of the Apec Economic Leaders’ Meeting in Shenzhen in November.

See also: China passenger vehicle retail sales drop 24% in September

China first signalled an opening in the sector in June 2015, announcing that foreign bank card clearing providers could apply for licenses by establishing local units or through acquisitions. The move was designed to dismantle the long-standing monopoly held by state-run China UnionPay Co.

While the approval marks a significant milestone, Visa is entering a market that looks very different from the one it first sought to enter. China’s payments ecosystem is now dominated by domestic mobile platforms Alipay and WeChat Pay, which have largely bypassed traditional card networks and become the primary channels for everyday transactions.

China had 10.2 billion bank cards in circulation at the end of 2025, with transaction value totalling 963.6 trillion yuan last year, according to the People’s Bank of China.

title: World economy holds up but nears limits of resilience, IMF says
article:
(Oct 13): The International Monetary Fund (IMF) said global growth should pick up next year with a boost from AI investment, but warned the world economy is nearing the limits of its resilience as the energy squeeze persists and financial risks build.

Growth will accelerate to 3.4% in 2027, the fund said Tuesday in its World Economic Outlook. That’s unchanged from the last update in July, while the forecast for this year was raised slightly to 3.1%.

Businesses “have continued to adjust to repeated shocks” while markets — buoyed by an exuberant tech industry — have taken a “broadly benign view of the challenges,” the IMF said.

But it also outlined several reasons why that may not last.

The world has run down its energy inventories to absorb supply shortages since the US attacked Iran, and those buffers could wear thin as the conflict drags on. The artificial intelligence boom has powered demand for hardware and could deliver broad gains in productivity, but it comes with financial risks attached. And the recent surge in bond yields makes it urgent to trim budget deficits and public debts.

See also: HSBC moves to Wall Street bonus model, cuts fixed-pay deals

“The global economy has been resilient but that resilience its reaching its limits” and risks to growth are tilted to the downside, IMF chief economist Silvana Tenreyro said.

Even with next year’s expected rebound, global growth would be lagging the 3.5% average over the previous two years, and the fund described medium-term prospects as “lackluster.”

See also: Healey needs £35 bil to meet UK spending plans, institute says

One reason is that the boost from AI is so uneven, and the report highlights gaps that are opening up as the technology advances. Almost two-thirds of the extra trade in computing hardware is sourced from just two countries, Taiwan and South Korea, according to the IMF. Meanwhile the US and China accounted for more than 75% of net AI-related imports last year.

The result is that global economic growth rests on a narrower base. Only 32 economies now account for 95% of the overall expansion, the IMF said, compared with 54 countries six months ago.

Whether the surge in AI-related demand “will transform into a positive supply shock in the long term by delivering faster productivity growth remains to be seen,” the IMF said. Meanwhile it’s “contributing to inflationary pressures and financial fragility.”

Still, the fund expects inflation to slow down next year. It forecasts that the global headline rate will fall back to 4.1% — where it was in 2025 — after spiking to 4.7% this year.

As for the budget challenges highlighted by the bond-market slump, the IMF said there’s an urgent need for “credible adjustment plans” to restore fiscal buffers.

“The task ahead is to move from coping to rebuilding,” Tenreyro said.

To stay ahead of Singapore and the region’s corporate and economic trends, click here for Latest Section

The expected pickup in growth next year hinges on an acceleration in emerging and developed economies. In the advanced ones, the IMF sees the expansion slowing to 1.8%, from 2.1% this year.

It predicts growth of 2.3% in the US, the world’s biggest economy — a slight upgrade to the 2.2% forecast in July. For China the 2027 forecast is unchanged at 4%.

Among major economies, the hit to France stands out. Its economy is set to expand only 0.4% this year and 0.7% in 2027. Both figures are 0.2 percentage point lower than in the fund’s July forecasts.

Germany is expected to grow 1.1% in 2027, while growth in the UK will edge down to 1.2% as energy prices and high interest rates weigh on consumption.

title: Trump’s diesel deal irks allies and is unlikely to reduce prices
article:
(Oct 13): US President Donald Trump’s deal for Russian diesel exposed the US to legal questions, opened a rift with his Republican allies and European leaders and heightened tensions with Ukraine — all in exchange for an outcome that experts suggest is unlikely to succeed.

Under the agreement — announced late last week — Russian President Vladimir Putin would begin releasing diesel supplies into global markets as part of a US effort to bring down prices from their record highs before the Nov 3 midterm elections. Trump has also intensified demands on Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy to stop attacking Russian refineries and announced an energy ceasefire between the two sides.

The decisions and the ceasefire are all a bet that lowering fuel prices will be the best way to win more votes next month despite the risk of a backlash from political friends and foes alike. On Sunday, a bipartisan group of senators argued that Trump should “reverse course” on his plan to cut a diesel deal with Russia.

“The United States should not provide Putin with a financial lifeline while Russia continues to kill Ukrainian civilians,” the senators said in a statement.

The accord also provoked fresh tension with Europe, where officials warned that it would bolster Moscow’s war effort in Ukraine. They said the US should impose more sanctions instead.

“We would call on the US to put the sanctions in place so that actually we could finish this war, so that all the effects of these attacks on refineries would not be there,” top European Union diplomat Kaja Kallas told reporters in Luxembourg on Monday before meeting with the bloc’s foreign ministers.

See also: Trump lifts sanctions, says Russia to supply diesel to US, world

There’s also the legal challenge. A 2022 law prohibits the US from buying most Russian energy products. It’s still not clear how Trump plans to get around that, and some lawmakers, including Senator Roger Wicker, a Mississippi Republican, have already said they don’t expect the deal to go through.

Trump acknowledged on Monday that neither side had actually committed to stop attacking each other’s energy infrastructure.

“They agreed. You know why? Because I said you agree,” Trump told reporters. “That’s why they agreed — because I said they agreed.”

See also: Australia says doesn’t need Russian fuel after Trump diesel move

“I think actually Putin wants to make a deal more than Zelenskyy,” Trump said.

Keith Kellogg, the president’s former envoy to Kyiv, dismissed Trump’s latest disagreement with Zelenskyy as “noise.” He said he didn’t expect it to escalate to anything similar to their infamous face-to-face argument in the Oval Office in February 2025.

“The rhetoric will kind of take care of itself,” Kellogg said. “Look at what’s happening on the ground.”

That’s all in exchange for an effort to bring down global diesel prices that have remained stubbornly high, mostly because of the Iran war, which has throttled traffic through the Strait of Hormuz. Russia’s conflict with Ukraine also played a role, after Russia extended a ban on diesel exports through September following a wave of Ukrainian drone strikes on the country’s refineries.

Unfortunately for Trump, even if Russian diesel reaches the global market in the coming weeks, it probably won’t offer much relief for American farmers and truckers before the midterms.

The first release of 2.25 million barrels in October is 1.4 million barrels less than American consumers used in a single day as of early in the month. Shipments from Russia to the East Coast typically take more than two weeks, and record-high shipping costs would also likely push prices higher.

If Russian refineries are able to resume some exports, it would provide marginal relief to a global oil market that’s sorely missed the supply, analysts say. Yet whether those shipments restart in earnest depends on the durability of an energy ceasefire that Trump announced over the weekend. Neither Russia nor Ukraine said they had agreed to such a deal.

To stay ahead of Singapore and the region’s corporate and economic trends, click here for Latest Section

Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak said monthly diesel exports of three million tons — near levels seen before Ukraine’s drone campaign — will only be possible after December.

“There is no indication that any diesel is making its way to the US just yet,” Bloomberg geoeconomics analyst Alex Kokcharov wrote in a note. “Given questions around the legality of easing sanctions and Russia’s own export capacity, it’s not clear this will result in any net increase to global diesel supplies.”

title: Thailand eyes US$30 departure tax for tourists in revenue push
article:
(Oct 13): Thailand is looking to travellers for more revenue, testing a tourism industry that has yet to fully recover from the pandemic.

Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul’s government is considering an outbound tax of about 1,000 baht (US$30 or $38) on Thai and foreign travellers leaving the country, while separately planning a 450-baht fee for foreign visitors arriving by air.

The measures highlight a difficult trade-off for an economy already struggling with subdued domestic demand and sluggish growth. Thailand needs to raise more revenue after years of budget deficits of about 3%-4% of gross domestic product have eroded its fiscal space. But tourism is a major source of jobs, spending and foreign-currency earnings.

The Thai Travel Agents Association warned the outbound tax could sharply reduce passenger numbers, prompting airlines to cut flight frequencies and ultimately hurting inbound tourism. Such an outcome would also run counter to the government’s ambition to turn Thailand into a regional aviation hub, the group said.

Thailand welcomed about 24 million foreign tourists through Oct 10, down 4% from a year earlier and still well below the nearly 40 million recorded in 2019 before the pandemic. The Tourism Authority of Thailand expects about 33 million visitors this year. A total below last year’s 32.97 million would mark the first back-to-back annual decline outside the pandemic since at least 1995.

The proposed departure tax would revive a levy last set at 500 baht about two decades ago, said Finance Ministry Permanent Secretary Lavaron Sangsnit. Existing law allows the government to charge as much as 5,000 baht, though Lavaron said the rate under consideration is around 1,000 baht.

See also: American Airlines to expand Starlink WiFi across entire fleet

The tax could be incorporated into airline tickets rather than collected separately at departure, Lavaron said. He argued that people who can afford to travel overseas have greater ability to bear the additional cost, with proceeds potentially used to promote domestic tourism and fund travel insurance or emergency medical coverage.

The government also plans to charge foreign visitors arriving by air 450 baht, according to Tourism and Sports Minister Surasak Phancharoenworakul. More than 80% of respondents supported the proposal in a recent online public consultation, he said.

title: Marco Polo Marine CEO’s father increases stake in company
article:
Shares of Marco Polo Marine (MPM) have seen weakness in recent weeks, dipping below 12 cents on some days.

Presumably seeing an opportunity to scoop up shares on the cheap, Lee Wan Teng, the founder of MPM and father of current CEO Sean Lee, has purchased 1.7 million shares for $202,045, or at an average price of 11.885 cents per share, from the open market.

This raises the elder Lee’s direct and deemed interest in MPM to 13.49%, up from the previous 13.45%.

For 3QFY2026 ended June 30, MPM reported y-o-y revenue growth of 13% to $35.7 million, lifting 9MFY2026 revenue by 30% y-o-y to $109.7 million. Gross profit for the quarter and nine months respectively was up 7% y-o-y to $15 million and 30% y-o-y to $46.4 million.

The company is in the process of several corporate actions. On Sept 7, Fuji Offset Plates Manufacturing moved ahead with the planned $139 million reverse takeover deal of MPM’'s shipyard business.

Offshore wind company PKR Offshore, in which MPM owns a 49% stake, had also planned to submit its application for a listing on the Taiwanese stock exchange during the third quarter. However, no announcement has been made as yet of the submission.

See also: Q&M’s Ng in married deal with IOI Properties’ non-independent non-executive director involving 14 mil shares

As at 10.13am on Oct 13, shares in Marco Polo Marine are flat at 12 cents.

title: DayOne inks multi-currency financing arrangement with seven banks
article:
Singapore-headquartered data centre operator DayOne has secured a multi-currency financing arrangement with a consortium of seven banks. Its members include: CIMB, Crédit Agricole CIB, DBS Group (DBS) (SGX:D05 ) , Maybank, Oversea-Chinese Banking Corporation (OCBC) (SGX:O39 ) , Standard Chartered and the United Overseas Bank (UOB) (SGX:U11 ) .

The financing arrangement comprises a US$2.4 billion ($3.1 billion) offshore term loan facility as well as a RM5.5 billion ($1.7 billion) Murabahah facility agreement, adding up to RM15 billion. A Murabahah facility agreement is an Islamic financing structure that does not charge interest. Instead, it is a cost-plus financing arrangement where the bank buys an asset on behalf of its client and sells it back to them with a markup.

With this new financing arrangement, DayOne’s total financing now stands at RM30 billion. This includes the RM15 billion of multi-currency financing it secured last year. The additional financing will help support the company’s continued development of its data centre operations in Johor, Malaysia.

On Oct 6, DayOne announced that it had filed for an IPO on the Nasdaq. Previously in May, Reuters, citing an unnamed source, reported that the company was considering a US$5 billion dual listing on the Nasdaq and Singapore Exchange (SGX).

title: Australia regulator halts another credit fund amid crackdown
article:
(Oct 13): Australia’s securities regulator temporarily barred Fidante Partners Ltd from offering units in a credit fund, extending a clampdown on private credit investments amid concerns over risks to investors.

The Australian Securities and Investments Commission (Asic) issued a 21-day interim stop order against Class A units of the Ares Global Credit Income Fund, citing deficiencies in how the product’s target investors were identified. The regulator questioned whether the fund was suitable for investors seeking to preserve capital, as well as provisions allowing investors to allocate as much as 50% of their investable assets to the product.

The move comes just days after ASIC imposed interim stop orders on three mortgage investment funds operated by Australian Secure Capital Fund, which collectively manage about A$250 million (US$174 million). Those orders followed concerns over inadequate disclosures about loan portfolios and the costs investors could face when exiting the funds, underscoring growing regulatory scrutiny of an industry facing questions over transparency and liquidity risks.

“Where ASIC identifies concerns that products may be reaching retail investors they were not designed for, we will use our regulatory tools to act swiftly to intervene early, disrupt poor practices and protect investors from potential harm,” the regulator said in a statement on Tuesday.

Ares Global Credit Income Fund, which had A$799.9 million under management as of June 30, invests in global bonds, syndicated loans, asset-backed securities and collateralised loan obligations, according to Asic.

Asic said its latest intervention was part of broader surveillance of private credit funds, focusing on how products are distributed to retail investors, as well as fees, profit margins and potential conflicts of interest.

See also: Europe’s troubled carmakers get China boost on way to Paris show

title: Goldman says markets underestimating how far yuan can rise
article:
(Oct 13): A stronger yuan is among the most underpriced scenarios in the world’s US$9.5 trillion ($12.2 trillion)-a-day foreign exchange market, according to Goldman Sachs Group Inc’s Kamakshya Trivedi.

China’s currency is undervalued by around 20% to 25%, an estimate the bank’s global head of foreign exchange, rates and emerging markets strategy research calls “conservative.” He added that the nation’s swelling trade surplus strengthens the case for appreciation.

Goldman sees the yuan strengthening to 6.40 per dollar from around 6.69 in a year’s time, with the firm’s fair-value metrics pointing to a six handle as a future possibility, Trivedi said in an interview last week. China’s currency last traded near 6 in early 2014 amid rapid hot money inflows.

“People underestimate how far this can move,” said Trivedi. “At every stage as we’ve shifted the forecast stronger, I think I’ve been surprised by the extent to which consensus and forward markets still haven’t caught up to that.”

“Our view is very simple: we think it will be a gradual process, but it’s going to be sustained,” he added.

Goldman’s view comes as China confronts growing criticism from major trading partners such as European nations that it is using an artificially weak currency to boost exports. Beijing has rejected such claims, arguing that exchange-rate adjustments won’t resolve structural imbalances in the global economy, while adding that China’s export strength stems from its rising industrial competitiveness.

See also: South Korean won hits two-year high on lower oil, dollar sales

International pressure on the yuan has intensified even as Chinese authorities have allowed it to rise against most major peers, with the tightly managed currency appreciating to a four-year high versus the dollar. The yuan’s strength makes it one of the few currencies positioned for more sustained appreciation at a time when the greenback has rebounded due to geopolitical tensions and stubborn inflation.

Trivedi said the magnitude of the yuan’s undervaluation would look “much bigger” when factoring in China’s current account and external balance performance. China’s trade surplus stood at US$805.5 billion for the first eight months of the year, official data showed.

“So to my mind, there is no question that currency is significantly undervalued,” he said.

See also: Yuan hits four-year high versus basket as PBOC backs FX policy

Trivedi said Chinese policymakers may be becoming more comfortable with further yuan appreciation, partly due to the importance of stable trade relations.

China staved off wider trade frictions with the European Union by agreeing to curb exports of hybrid vehicles following talks that ended Friday. The yuan has appreciated more than 8% against the euro this year.

Beijing’s growing ease with a stronger currency also reflects the changing nature of the country’s export machine that is increasingly powered by cutting-edge technologies and advanced manufacturing.

“If you think about it even from China’s perspective, I think what is most important to them is the stability of trading relationships,” he said. “The longer you get stability in the trading relationships, I think they recognise that some degree of appreciation in the currency is consistent with the underlying macro.”

“China’s growing role as a provider of global funding marks a new phase of yuan internationalisation, extending the currency’s reach beyond trade settlement and payments into global borrowing, investment and hedging markets,” said Bloomberg strategists.

Trivedi also sees a stronger yuan aligning with Beijing’s goal of boosting the currency’s global role. Chinese President Xi Jinping had previously pledged to build a powerful currency that is widely used in international trade, investment and foreign exchange markets, holding the status of a global reserve currency.

“Modest, gradual but sustained appreciation I think serves that purpose of internationalisation as well,” Trivedi said. “It makes the return picture in Chinese assets a bit more attractive.”

title: Singapore bank sell-off tests city-state’s safe haven status
article:
(Oct 13): A sell-off in Singapore bank shares driven by fears of earnings downgrades is threatening one of Asia’s best-performing major stock benchmarks this year, putting the city-state’s safe haven status to the test.

The Straits Times Index has slid 6.6% from its peak more than five weeks ago, dragged lower by DBS Group Holdings Ltd, Oversea-Chinese Banking Corp and United Overseas Bank Ltd. The lenders account for more than half of the benchmark and shed a combined US$22.4 billion ($28.7 billion) in market value last week alone.

The sell-off reflects growing concern that local banks are entering a tougher phase ahead. Elevated bond yields are eroding the appeal of their dividend payouts, while the lenders will also have to account for losses on their holdings. That’s prompted Wall Street brokers to warn of downside risks to earnings released next month.

“The risk is a longer sell-off that spreads beyond the banks, or earnings and capital returns that start to weaken,” said Alex Ho, a sales trader at CMC Markets Singapore. “November’s results will be the first real test.”

Prior to the recent slump, Singapore stocks had hit a string of highs as earnings growth and market stability attracted institutional investors seeking shelter from gyrations tied to the escalating Iran war and AI trade. Investors are now backing away, with analysts increasingly wary about expectations remaining too optimistic into year end.

See also: Singapore power rates to fall from record after fuel price drop

JPMorgan Chase & Co warned on Wednesday that rising long bond yields will result in high mark-to-market losses on banks’ trading books and hurt capital activity for Southeast Asian banks. Separately, Citigroup Inc downgraded OCBC to ‘sell’ and iterated its ‘sell’ on UOB last week. HSBC Holdings Plc has also cut Singapore stocks to ‘neutral’ as valuations become stretched and financial conditions weigh on the real estate sector.

The strong rally in Singapore banks earlier this year has made the sector an outlier when compared with regional and global peers on a valuation perspective. Even after the recent pullback, DBS — the country’s largest lender — trades at 16.9 times its 12-month forward earnings compared with 13.2 times for MSCI financials gauge.

Not everyone is turning cautious, though. Some strategists argue that Singapore’s growth prospects coupled with the government’s efforts to rejuvenate the equities market should limit downside risks, even if the jury is out on the moves in the shorter term.

See also: You don’t need deep pockets to survive in F&B

“Critically, there are still no overtly concerning signs of bad debt, which tend to characterize bear markets for the banks, while loan growth is relatively healthy,” according to Jen-Ai Chua, Asia equity research analyst at Julius Baer. “As we enter the traditionally turbulent month of October, the only thing we can be sure of is more volatility in price action ahead,” she said.

title: Jardine Matheson raises underlying earnings guidance for FY2026; assumes full control of Gammon Construction
article:
Jardine Matheson has raised its FY2026 earnings guidance to reflect "continued solid performance" across its portfolio.

From US$5.33 per share, Jardine Matheson now expects its underlying earnings per share to reach between US$5.50 and US$5.65. This metric is adjusted for disposals and reclassifications in the preceding FY2025.

Jardines Matheson will provide its regular interim update on Nov 20.

In addition, Jardine Matheson has completed the acquisition of a 50% stake in Gammon Construction previously held by its JV partner Balfour Beatty for US$330 million.

Jardines has been an investor in Gammon since 1969 and with full ownership of this entity, expects "modestly accretive" earnings from its first year.

Lincoln Pan, CEO of Jardine Matheson calls Gammon Construction the second "significant transaction" in 2026 and is a strategic, synergistic expansion of its Jardine Engineering & Infrastructure vertical.

See also: Amazon in talks to buy AI startup Decart, WSJ reports

"Our goal remains doubling the earnings of JE&I in the coming years by focusing on strategic investments that expand controlled earnings and capabilities across Asia," he adds.

Kevin O’Brien, CEO of Jardine Engineering & Infrastructure, calls Gammon Construction a "high-quality business with a strong reputation, deep customer relationships and talented people."

He sees significant opportunities for Gammon across the region, such as projects in Hong Kong's Northern Metropolis, as well as in Singapore and the wider region.

See also: StarHub takes tentative step towards industry consolidation with acquisition of MyRepublic's mobile business

In his Oct 13 note, Jayden Vantarakis of Macquarie points out that Gammon sits within the Jardine Engineering division, which was formerly part of Jardine Pacific, and held entirely at the hold-co level.

He figures that these businesses account for 7% of his gross estimated net asset value of the company.

He notes that Jardine Matheson did not split out the contribution of each of the three engineering entities, except that in total, earnings was up 13% in the most recent 1HFY2026.

According to Vantarakis, Gammon has been a steady contributor of earnings, providing US$53 million PATMI to Jardine Matheson in FY2025, and he calculates a 6 times trailing P/E acquisition multiple.

The acquisition, points out the analyst, is inclusive of all future dividend entitlements and cash on Gammon's balance sheet.

Vantarakis observes that this deal is consistent with what Jardine Matheson had indicated in its 2026 strategy day, where the company aims to double the profit contribution of its engineering entities by FY2030 over FY2025 levels, where patmi reached US$1.95 million.

The growth will be eked via a combination of acquisitions and organic expansion.
